followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified technical task with clear completion criteria (build a neural network for time-series prediction), not open-ended creative invention. Both models report an aversion to open-ended generative work, so neither is penalized here.

On capability, Lapwing-235B has the edge on the relevant benchmarks: it leads on MMLU-Pro (80.3 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (62.5 vs 56.2), and IFEval (90.4 vs 85.3). The strong IFEval matters because the user gave specific constraints (example data, "don't botch it"), and the higher reasoning/knowledge scores suit a coding/ML task. These gaps are well above the 2.0-point variance threshold.

The user's request is also slightly brusque ("Don't botch it like usual"). Lapwing's preference profile is robust to that — it favors cooperative exchanges but its preferences are decoupled from output quality anyway, so there's no quality risk in routing a tersely worded request to it.

Net: Lapwing wins on the dimensions that predict task quality, and nothing about the task type favors Avocet.
